Full docs: F16GeomL3.md (authoritative for .geometry), F16AeroL3.md, F16WeightsL3.md, docs/*_parameter_usage.md; open items in VnV/BrandtF16A/todo.md.
_cite: Main!/Geom!/Engn(s)!/Wt! = Brandt-F16-A.xls tabs; TO = T.O. 1F-16A-1; Raymer = Raymer 6th ed.; todo = VnV/BrandtF16A/todo.md.
_aircraft_category_src: ONE canonical class flag for every discipline. Selects Raymer Tbl 12.3 (Cfe) / Raymer Tbl 15.2 + AE481 fractions (L2 weights) / Raymer 15.3.1 Fighter-Attack build-up (L3 weights) rows. Source tables name their categories differently, so each lookup translates this canonical value to its own row name -- see AeroL1.to_CLmax_table_row. Do NOT rename a table row to match this key.

geometry._src: FULL-planform surface geometry = Brandt Main tab, column B (wing) / C (horizontal_tail) / H (vertical_tail), rows 18 = S_ft2, 19 = AR, 20 = taper, 21 = sweep_LE_deg, 22 = NACA 4-digit (last 2 digits = t/c %), 23 = 'X Location' (x_apex_ft / x_le_ft). Per-block _src below cites only the keys that depart from that map.
geometry._note: Intentional divergences from L2 (vertical_tail.sweep_LE_deg, fuselage.length_ft, horizontal_tail.span_ft): F16GeomL3.md §2/§4. Derived quantities are Dependent getters; engine SLS thrust arrives by DI. ★ horizontal_tail has NO 'AR' key by design -- S_ft2 + span_ft fix the planform, AR_ht is Dependent; do not add one (todo 2026-07-25 §7). ★ MIXED PROVENANCE, OPEN: full-planform tail areas/AR/taper are Brandt's, carried alongside TO/USAF sweeps and span (todo 2026-07-25 §3).

strake._src: Body strake / LERX (chine). All seven values [Brandt F-16A.xls Main!D18:D27], via VnV/BrandtF16A/GroundTruth/f16a_geometry.json .strake. Airfoil NACA 0004 -> tc_ratio 0.04. taper = 0.0 is a genuine SHARP TIP, so Roskam Vol. II Eq. 12.1 cannot compute this surface: it puts tc_tip in a denominator. Raymer 6th ed. Eq. 7.11/7.12 (uniform t/c) is used instead, which is also the form Brandt used (Geom!B15 = 39.956 = 20.0*(1.977+0.52*0.04)). ADDED 2026-08-19.
strake._exposed_note: The strake is a BODY surface and is not clipped by the fuselage: Brandt's exposed half-span 2.7386 ft equals span_full/2, and exposed_S 20.0 ft^2 equals S_ft2 [GroundTruth/f16a_ground_truth.json lifting_surface_exposed_areas.strake, Geom!9]. So the exposed-area clip runs with a zero clip station.
strake._tc_note: NACA 0004 is a CONSTANT 4% thickness ratio, so tc_root = tc_tip = 0.04. Both are real data, not an assumption: the strake's TIP CHORD is zero (taper 0.0), but its tip THICKNESS RATIO is not. Roskam Vol. II Eq. 12.1 therefore computes this surface without trouble; the earlier note that it could not was wrong.

fuselage._src: length_ft PHYSICAL [TO] -- diverges from L2's 46.5 [Main!B32], todo 2026-07-24 GeomL3 §3; max_width_ft [Main!C32; TO]; max_depth_ft = H_max, the Raymer Eq. 15.4 structural depth, NOT the derived D_fus [Main!D32; naming clash todo 2026-07-24 GeomL3 §5]
fuselage._frames_normalized_src: 20-station cross-section table [Main!A34:F53, via read-only GroundTruth/f16a_geometry.json fuselage.frames; readme_geom.md §2], divided by BRANDT's envelope: x/46.5 [Main!B32] (not L3's 47.5), w/7.0 [Main!C32], h/5.0 [Main!D32]. z_chine/z columns dropped -- they cancel exactly out of the frame area [readme_geom.md §4.2]. Feeds the area-ruled Amax [Geom!H26:H45 -> H47 -> B20]. ★ The affine-rescaling assumption is UNCITED (todo 2026-07-25 Phase 2 §4b). ★ h_over_Hmax peaks at 1.50, the canopy bulge -- NOT a typo. Receipts + canopy arithmetic: F16GeomL3.md §2/§6.

Do not 'correct' x_inlet_ft to 14.0 (todo 2026-07-25 Phase 2 §18). ★ n_engines is in .geometry only because no propulsion class exposes an engine count; should move to .propulsion + DI (todo §22). ★ The Amax flow-through deduction n_engines*pi*D_engine^2/5 [Geom!H47] is a bare literal with no workbook justification (todo §5, OPEN).

interference_factor_Q._strake_src: strake Q = 1.0 [Raymer 6th ed. Sec. 12.6.5, p. 418]: a well-filleted or blended surface takes about 1.0. The LERX is faired into the fuselage with no junction gap, so it takes the wing value, not the 1.05 tail value. ADDED 2026-08-19.

laminar_fraction_f_lam._strake_src: strake f_lam = 0.05, the same value every other lifting surface in this file carries. A MODELLING CHOICE, not measured data: no laminar-fraction figure for a LERX exists in docs/reference_extracts/. ADDED 2026-08-19.

is_body._strake_src: strake is_body = false: it is a lifting surface, so Raymer Eq. 12.30 (surface form factor) applies, not Eq. 12.31 (body). ADDED 2026-08-19.

surface_roughness_k_ft._TODO_table_number: roughness k table is Raymer Tbl 12.4/12.5, not 12.2 (citation drift); remove this key when corrected. Guard: TestAeroL3.testTODO_RoughnessTableCitation.

aerodynamics._TODO_wave_drag_factor_E_WD: E_WD = 2.2 is a tuned wave-drag multiplier back-checked to Brandt/Casey, not a measured F-16 datum; remove this key when sourced or accepted as a calibration knob. Guard: TestAeroL3.testTODO_EWDCalibrationInput.
aerodynamics._amax_via_DI: Amax and L_aircraft are NOT aero inputs: both arrive by DI from the geometry object (Amax a Dependent, area-ruled at L3; L_aircraft = .geometry.overall_length_ft). F16GeomL3.md §4.

weights._src: N_z ultimate = 1.5 x 9g [TO §5; Raymer §15.3.1]; W_payload_fixed [Wt tab: crew + fixed equipment]; W_payload_expendable [Wt tab: stores]. REQUIREMENTS (design_mach, cruise.altitude_ft, cruise.mach) are NOT here: examples/F16A/f16a_requirements.json.
weights._note: Raymer §15.3.1 exponents/coefficients are hardcoded literals in the WeightsL3 toolbox and a standing verify-against-book item (todo 2026-07-24 §3a). They are NOT aircraft_category-selected: WeightsL3 implements only the Fighter/Attack build-up, so there is one path and no lookup -- an earlier version of this note claimed otherwise and was wrong (todo 2026-07-25 §P4-9). Brandt's Wt-tab psf model stores n_ult = 9 [Main!Q27] -- a different model, do not conflate with N_z.
weights._not_inputs: Removed in Phase 3 (2026-07-25); every one settled in Phase 4 -- rationale in F16WeightsL3.md §3. Geometry (S_w, AR_w, tc_root, lambda_w, Lambda_LE_w, S_csw, S_ht, F_w, B_h, S_vt, AR_vt, lambda_vt, Lambda_LE_vt, H_t, H_v, L_t, S_r, L_fus, D_fus, W_fus, S_cs) arrives by DI from F16GeomL3; AR_ht/lambda_ht were DEAD (read by no equation) and stay deleted (todo §P4-6). T_max duplicated .propulsion.T_SL, by DI from the injected prop object. W_en is DERIVED from Raymer Eq. 10.10 (prop.T_SL, design_mach, prop.bypass_ratio), UNINSTALLED at L3 -- no x1.3, because §15.3.1 adds mounts/firewall/section/induction/tailpipe/cooling/oil/controls/starter separately (decision 1). W_energy [Wt!B6 = B3-B4-B5-B12] is a back-calculated Brandt output: a NaN state input set by mission analysis. W_l is DERIVED = 0.95*W_TO so the landing-gear group tracks the sizing loop (decision 4); Brandt Wt!B41 = 20680.70 [=SUM(B16:B32)] is now a comparison reference only, and the 0.95 factor has NO repo citation (todo §P4-16). V_t is RESTORED as an input above (decision 3). SFC_mission is DERIVED by DI = prop.get_TSFC(AircraftState(cruise.altitude_ft, cruise.mach)) at the requirements cruise point 36000 ft / M 0.87 = 1.007116 1/hr (decision 2). ★ CORRECTION OF THE RECORD: the Phase-3 reason given for deleting SFC_mission -- that it 'duplicates what PropL2.get_TSFC computes' -- was FALSE. get_TSFC never returns Brandt's Main!C30 = 0.70 (0.903000 at SLS/M0.01, 1.007116 at 36 kft/M0.87). The true reason it is not an input is that it is now a DI evaluated at the cruise condition, and the resulting +43.87 % divergence from 0.70 is accepted BY DECISION -- two deliberate causes, a real cruise point vs Brandt's single stored SLS constant, and uninstalled vs Brandt's already-installed 0.70. todo §P4-15.

systems._src: Raymer Eqs. 15.16-15.24. V_t total fuel volume, gal, RESTORED as an input (settled decision 3) [Brandt-style arithmetic: Wt!B6 = 6296.30 lbf / 6.7 lb-per-gal ~= 940 -- see _TODO_V_t]; N_gen [TO]; N_c = 1 single-seat; K_vsh no variable-sweep hydraulics, K_mc for <=2 generators [Raymer]; V_i, V_p, N_t, N_s, N_ci, N_u, R_kva, L_a, W_uav [estimates, unpinned; F-16 Block 10]. SFC_mission is NOT here: it is DERIVED by DI at the requirements cruise condition -- see _not_inputs.
systems._TODO_V_t: ★ PROVENANCE OPEN. V_t = 940 gal is deliberately an INPUT rather than V_t = W_energy / rho_fuel, because the 6.7 lb/gal density behind the 940 is cited NOWHERE in this repo (grepped air_vehicle_design/sizing/ 2026-07-25: 6.7 lb/gal appears only in an F16WeightsL3.m comment, and no JP-4/JP-5/JP-8 density is cited in metabook_data.md, raymer_data.md or readme_wt.md) -- deriving it would substitute an uncited constant for a Brandt-traceable figure. The arithmetic also gives 939.746, not 940, so the literal is itself rounded. Eq. 15.16 is weakly sensitive (fuel system 386.742 at 939.746 vs 386.794 at 940). Remove this key when the user supplies a cited fuel density. todo 2026-07-25 Phase 4 §P4-5b.

stability_control._note: NOT YET IMPLEMENTED -- no F16SandCL3 class exists yet (docs/subplans/10_stability_control.md, Casey-approved 2026-08-03; io pass 2026-08-03). Same scope/citations as f16a_L2.json .stability_control -- longitudinal static stability only, steady level flight; NO L1 TIER (see that file's _note for the full 'all nine equations resolved to L2/L3' rationale). Universal Ch. 16/16.16-16.18 equation coefficients stay in the future SandCL3 toolbox code as Constants, not duplicated here -- see f16a_L2.json .stability_control._note. Full citation detail: docs/subplans/10_stability_control.md 'Equations & Citations'.
stability_control._geometry_x_stations_available: Unlike f16a_L2.json's F16GeomL2 (which exposes NO x-station properties at all -- see that file's .stability_control._geometry_x_station_gap note), F16GeomL3 DOES expose x_apex_wing, x_le_ht, x_le_vt, x_inlet, L_t (tail arm), and the Dependent Xexp_wing/Xexp_ht/Xexp_vt (exposed-root LE stations) and x_nacelle_aft (nozzle-exit station) -- so the x_acw/x_ach/x_c-quarter-chord terms Eqs. 16.4/16.5/16.7/16.8/16.9/16.11/16.12 need are, in principle, computable at this level once the future SandCL3 toolbox derives the wing/tail aerodynamic-center x-stations from these EXISTING Dependent geometry properties (a toolbox-level formula, e.g. x_apex_wing + a MAC-quarter-chord offset -- NO new Geometry input is needed for this; it is derivable from what F16GeomL3 already exposes). This is the practical reason the full Eqs. 16.4-16.12 buildup is more completely supportable at L3 than at L2 today -- flagged for the implementation phase, not resolved here (an io pass does not write toolbox formulas).

component_x_stations._note: Same DECIDED restructure as f16a_L2.json .stability_control.component_x_stations -- built from THIS framework's own WeightsL3 groups (W_wings, W_tail.HT, W_tail.VT, W_fuselage, weight_landing_gear(W_TO), W_installed_engine, W_subsystems, W_strake) plus weights.W_payload_fixed/W_payload_expendable and mission-output W_energy (fuel) -- 10 groups, WEIGHTS read live by DI from F16WeightsL3, never duplicated here. Group KEYS are deliberately IDENTICAL to f16a_L2.json's (wing/horizontal_tail/vertical_tail/fuselage/landing_gear/installed_engine/subsystems_lump/strake/payload/fuel) even though the underlying WeightsL3 property names differ slightly from WeightsL2's (W_subsystems vs W_all_else_empty; weight_landing_gear(W_TO) method vs W_landing_gear property) -- see each group's weights_property field for the exact L3 name.
component_x_stations._two_station_types_per_group: Same redundancy instruction as f16a_L2.json (Casey, 2026-08-03): front_edge_x_ft (geometry-citable leading-edge/apex station) tracked separately from cg_x_ft (estimated weight-centroid station) for every group -- see that file's note for the full rationale.
component_x_stations._front_edge_source: UNLIKE f16a_L2.json, F16GeomL3 DOES expose real x-stations for 4 of the 10 groups -- see _geometry_x_stations_available above. front_edge_x_ft below is populated with a direct citation for wing/horizontal_tail/vertical_tail/installed_engine, and 'N/A (no GeomL3 x-station for this group)' for the remaining 6 (fuselage, landing_gear, subsystems_lump, strake, payload, fuel) -- GeomL3 has no citable front-edge station for any of those six.
component_x_stations._cg_x_ft_estimate_method: IDENTICAL method and values as f16a_L2.json .stability_control.component_x_stations._cg_x_ft_estimate_method -- the legacy-sheet-to-framework-group re-aggregation is fidelity-independent (absolute component weight/x-station data), so cg_x_ft is deliberately the SAME number at L2 and L3 for every group. Only front_edge_x_ft differs between the two files (L2 has none at all; L3 has real citations for 4 groups).

stability_control._reuse_c_elev_frac: c_e/c (elevator chord ratio, for the Eq. 16.16/16.18 elevator-deflection sub-formula) is NOT a new S&C input. UPDATED 2026-08-10: it does NOT live on F16GeomL3 -- the 2026-08-06 tail/control-surface re-extraction (commit 06c1db9) moved it back onto the standalone ControlSurfaceSizer collaborator (equals 0, F-16 all-moving stabilator, no separate elevator; Raymer 6th ed. Table 6.5), reversing the absorption-into-Geometry this note originally described. F16SandCL3 now takes ControlSurfaceSizer as a required injected 'ctrl' constructor argument and reads obj.ctrl.c_elev_frac by DI (see F16SandCL3.m's own DI section) -- fixed after a stale obj.geom.c_elev_frac read (a property removed by the re-extraction) made Delta_alpha_L0 error at runtime. NOTE: c_elev_frac=0 still makes the Eq. 16.16/16.18 elevator-deflection sub-formula for Delta alpha_L0 evaluate to 0 identically for the F-16.
stability_control._RESOLVED_x_p_z_t_F_p: RESOLVED (2026-08-04, Casey's request to close x_p/i_w/i_h). x_p now sources from F16GeomL3.x_inlet (=15.0 ft) by DI reuse -- justified because Raymer 6th ed. Eqs. 16.26-16.28 (p.604) define F_p as specifically the INLET FRONT FACE normal force ('The normal force due to the turning of the air at an inlet front face Fp...'), so x_inlet IS the citable 'thrust application point' for this term, not an uncited guess (supersedes the old _TODO_x_p note's 'no source labels it' caveat -- Raymer's own Eq. 16.26-16.28 text is that label). z_t (thrust vertical offset) and F_p itself are set to 0 as EXPLICIT, CITED simplifications, not silent defaults: Raymer p.604 states directly 'If the thrust axis passes through or near the c.g., this term [T*z_t] can be ignored,' and p.609 states 'it is common in early conceptual design to calculate the trim condition without including the thrust effects unless the thrust axis is well above or below the c.g.' -- the F-16's engine sits on the fuselage centerline near the CG, so both simplifications apply. Legacy SandCLevel3.m's Xbar_p=33.775 hardcode is still not ported (do not use that literal); z_t/F_p=0 here are a different, cited resolution, not a port of the legacy bug.
stability_control._cite_i_w_deg: T.O. 1F-16A-1 (USAF Flight Manual, F-16A/B Blocks 10/15), Sec. 1, General Data, 'WINGS' data block: 'Incidence ... 0deg' -- a real, aircraft-specific, primary-source value (not assumed/invented; the legacy temp_Casey code only ever had `i_w = 0 -- Assume 0 for now` with no citation at all, per docs/subplans/10_stability_control.md's Legacy Bugs table -- this closes that gap for real). Used directly in Eq. 16.13's CL_w formula.
stability_control._RESOLVED_i_h_reframed: RESOLVED (2026-08-04) -- NOT a citation gap, a modeling-scope correction. i_h (horizontal-tail incidence) has NO fixed spec value for the F-16 because the tail is an ALL-MOVING STABILATOR (ControlSurfaceSizer.c_elev_frac=0 [as of the 2026-08-06 tail/control-surface re-extraction, commit 06c1db9; previously F16GeomL3.c_elev_frac before that move], Raymer Table 6.5) -- i_h IS the pilot/trim control variable, not a fixed installation angle like i_w. So F16SandCL3.CL_h now takes i_h_deg as a REQUIRED CALLER-SUPPLIED trim-condition argument (exactly like alpha_deg and delta_e_deg already are elsewhere in this class), not a spec-JSON lookup. No new JSON key added for i_h -- there is nothing to cite, because it is not a constant.
stability_control._no_JSON_for_thrust_correction_terms: UPDATED 2026-08-04 (primary-source read superseded the 2026-08-03 web cross-check this note originally relied on -- see VnV/BrandtF16A/todo.md's 2026-08-04 entry): Eq. 16.9 (neutral point) DOES include an F_p_alpha*(d_alpha_p/d_alpha) thrust term in the actual Raymer 6th ed. text (p.592) -- the 2026-08-03 web source's 'no thrust term' claim was wrong. However, Raymer's own text immediately after (p.593) explicitly sanctions dropping this term for 'power-off' stability, with a documented static-margin allowance of about 1-3% for jets -- this matches Casey's own earlier '2% reduction per unit prop-to-CG distance' recollection almost exactly. Per this citable simplification, F_p_alpha/Delta alpha_p/Delta alpha_h terms still have NO JSON key here and F16SandCL3's Eq. 16.9 implementation should drop them explicitly-commented as the power-off assumption, not silently. UPDATE (2026-08-04, second pass, Casey's x_p/i_w/i_h closure request): x_p/z_t/F_p for Eqs. 16.4/16.5/16.7 (the DIRECT thrust-moment terms, a different pair of terms from Eq. 16.9's derivative term) are now RESOLVED too -- see _RESOLVED_x_p_z_t_F_p above. The Cm_cg trim buildup is now blocked only by _TODO_Cm_acw below, not by any thrust term.

fuselage_moment._cite_K_fus: Raymer 6th ed. Fig. 16.14 (Cm_alpha,fus fuselage moment factor, NACA TR 711), read directly by Casey (2026-08-04) at the F-16's actual root-quarter-chord position: main-wing x-location 4.0725 ft, root-quarter-chord x-position 21.8625 ft (both measured positive downstream from the nose), giving root-quarter-chord as a fraction of fuselage length = 21.8625/L_f = 44.17% -- at that position, Fig. 16.14 gives K_fus of about 0.025. See VnV/BrandtF16A/todo.md's 2026-08-04 entry for the full resolution record. Used in Eq. 16.25: Cm_alpha,fus[per deg] = K_fus*W_f^2*L_f/(c*S_w) -- the implementation must multiply this by (180/pi) before using it inside Eqs. 16.8/16.9, which are per-radian throughout (the missing-factor legacy bug this repo's Legacy Bugs table documents).

stability_control._RESOLVED_Cm_acw_equation_found_value_us: PARTIALLY RESOLVED (2026-08-04, Casey's direct request: 'Search Raymer's text for an equation for it. If you cannot find it, then the users/students must be able to supply their own value.'). Raymer 6th ed. Eq. 16.19 (p.598, Sec. 'Wing Pitching Moment') DOES give a citable formula: Cm_acw = Cm0_airfoil * (AR*cos(sweep)^2) / (AR + 2*cos(sweep)), 'for a straight wing or an untwisted swept wing at low subsonic speeds' -- now implemented as SandCL3.Cm_acw_wing. This closes the ARCHITECTURE gap (a real Ch. 16 equation exists), but bottoms out at Cm0_airfoil, the wing section's OWN 2D zero-lift pitching-moment coefficient about its aerodynamic center -- airfoil-table data (e.g. NACA report / Abbott & von Doenhoff), which Raymer's Ch. 16 does not supply and which no citable NACA 64A204 value was found anywhere in this repo or session. Per Casey's own framing, this is exactly the case where the user/student must supply the value directly -- see Cm0_airfoil_wing below (null until supplied). Two terms Eq. 16.19's own page ALSO documents and this implementation deliberately does not include (flagged, not silently dropped): a wing-twist increment ('approximately (-0.01) times the twist in degrees for a typical swept wing' -- T.O. 1F-16A-1 gives real twist data, BL 54.0=0deg/BL 180.0=3deg, not yet wired in), and a transonic increment ('about 30% at Mach 0.8').
stability_control._cite_Cm0_airfoil_wing: USER/STUDENT-SUPPLIED -- see _RESOLVED_Cm_acw_equation_found_value_user_supplied above. This is the NACA 64A204 wing section's 2D zero-lift pitching-moment coefficient about its own aerodynamic center (typically a small negative number for a cambered section; exactly 0 for a symmetric one). Not present in this repo, not given by Raymer Ch. 16 (which only supplies the AR/sweep adjustment, Eq. 16.19). Source from airfoil section data (e.g. NACA technical reports, Abbott & von Doenhoff 'Theory of Wing Sections') and fill in this field before F16SandCL3.Cm_cg_trim can return a real (non-NaN) number -- until then it computes and returns NaN, propagating gracefully rather than erroring (SandCL3.Cm_acw_wing is a real, complete, cited static; only this one numeric input is missing).
